name.zh: 条形磁铁 A · 北极

summary.en: Pulls hardest here; points north when hung.
summary.zh: 这一端吸力最强；悬挂时指向北方。

detail.en:
The north-pole half of a steel bar magnet, 100 × 20 × 10 mm in this design [S1]. A magnet pulls hardest near its ends. Hung from a thread, this end turns to point north, which is how the north pole gets its name [S2].

The colour only marks the end; paint does not make a magnet work. Cut the bar in two and each piece still has a north pole and a south pole [S3].
detail.zh:
钢制条形磁铁的北极这一半，本设计尺寸 100 × 20 × 10 mm [S1]。磁铁两端附近吸力最强。用细线挂起来时，这一端转向北方，北极的名字就是这样来的 [S2]。

颜色只是标记，磁铁并不是因为涂了颜色才有磁性。把条形磁铁切成两段，每段仍各有北极和南极 [S3]。

name.zh: 条形磁铁 A · 南极

summary.en: Pulls hardest here; points south when hung.
summary.zh: 这一端吸力最强；悬挂时指向南方。

detail.en:
The south-pole half of the same bar magnet [S1]. It pulls as hard as the north pole. A south pole attracts a north pole and repels another south pole [S2].

The model draws the bar as two coloured halves so that each pole can be picked and labelled; a real bar magnet is one piece of steel [S1].
detail.zh:
同一根条形磁铁的南极这一半 [S1]。它的吸力和北极一样大。南极吸引北极，排斥另一个南极 [S2]。

模型把条形磁铁画成两段不同颜色，只是为了让两个磁极能分别点选和标注；真的条形磁铁是一整块钢 [S1]。

summary.en: Pulls or pushes magnet A across the gap.
summary.zh: 隔着间隙拉或推磁铁 A。

detail.en:
A second 100 mm bar magnet on a plastic guide, so that the gap to magnet A can be set to 6, 3 or 1.5 cm [S1]. With unlike poles facing it is pulled towards A; turned round, it is pushed away [S2].

In this model the pull at 6, 3 and 1.5 cm is 12, 41 and 100 percent of the pull at 1.5 cm [S1]. These are model numbers for comparing, not measurements.
detail.zh:
第二根 100 mm 的条形磁铁，放在一条塑料导轨上，和磁铁 A 的间隙可以设为 6、3 或 1.5 cm [S1]。异极相对时，它被拉向 A；调个头，它就被推开 [S2]。

在这个模型里，间隙 6、3、1.5 cm 时的拉力，分别是 1.5 cm 时的 12 %、41 %、100 % [S1]。这些是用来比较的模型数字，不是实测值。

summary.en: Brings both poles side by side.
summary.zh: 把两个磁极并排放在一起。

detail.en:
A magnet bent into a U, so that its north and south poles sit side by side at the open end. Paper clips cling to the pole tips, where the pull is strongest [S3].

Bending does not remove either pole: one tip is a north pole and the other a south pole [S3]. Its size is a design choice [S1].
detail.zh:
弯成 U 形的磁铁，北极和南极并排在开口的两端。回形针吸在两个极尖上，那里吸力最强 [S3]。

弯曲不会让任何一个磁极消失：一个极尖是北极，另一个是南极 [S3]。尺寸是本设计选定的 [S1]。

summary.en: Pushes the upper ring up, or pulls it down.
summary.zh: 把上面的环推起，或把它拉下。

detail.en: A flat ring magnet with its poles on its two flat faces, 30 mm across in this design [S1]. With like poles facing, it pushes the upper ring up so that it floats; turn the upper ring over and the two clamp together [S2].
detail.zh: 扁平的环形磁铁，两个磁极在上下两个平面上，本设计直径 30 mm [S1]。同极相对时，它把上面的环推起来，让它悬在空中；把上面的环翻过来，两只环就紧紧贴在一起 [S2]。

summary.en: Floats when like poles face.
summary.zh: 同极相对时悬在空中。

detail.en:
The same kind of ring magnet, threaded on the post above the lower one. With like poles facing, the push from the lower ring holds it up against its weight; in this model it floats about 1 cm above [S1].

Turned over, unlike poles face each other, the push becomes a pull and the ring drops onto the lower one [S2].
detail.zh:
同样的环形磁铁，套在立柱上、下面那只的上方。同极相对时，下面那只的推力托住它，不让它落下；在这个模型里，它悬在下面那只上方约 1 cm [S1]。

翻过来，异极相对，推力变成拉力，它就落到下面那只上 [S2]。

summary.en: Stops the floating ring sliding off.
summary.zh: 不让悬浮的环从旁边滑下。

detail.en: A wooden post through the middle of both rings. Wood is not a magnetic material, so the post does not pull on the rings [S2]. It only stops the upper ring sliding sideways: the ring is held up by the push between the magnets, not by the post [S1].
detail.zh: 一根穿过两只环中间的木柱。木头不是磁性材料，立柱不会吸引环 [S2]。它只是不让上面的环向旁边滑走：托住环的是两块磁铁之间的推力，不是立柱 [S1]。

summary.en: Holds the turning needle and its dial.
summary.zh: 装着能转动的磁针和刻度盘。

detail.en:
A round brass case, 50 mm across in this design [S1]. Brass is not attracted by a magnet, so the case does not turn the needle [S20].

The compass can be moved to eight spots round bar magnet A. At each spot the needle lines up with the pattern round the magnet [S5].
detail.zh:
圆形黄铜外壳，本设计直径 50 mm [S1]。黄铜不被磁铁吸引，所以外壳不会让磁针转动 [S20]。

指南针可以放到条形磁铁 A 周围的八个位置上，在每个位置，磁针都顺着磁铁周围的图样指 [S5]。

summary.en: Shows which way the needle points.
summary.zh: 显示磁针指向哪个方向。

detail.en:
A dial with 32 marks, four of them longer for north, east, south and west [S1]. The dial does not move; read the needle against it.

In this model north is towards the back of the bench [S1].
detail.zh:
刻度盘上有 32 条刻度，其中四条较长，分别对着北、东、南、西 [S1]。刻度盘不动，对照它读出磁针的方向。

在这个模型里，北方朝着实验台的后面 [S1]。

summary.en: Turns to line up with a magnet’s pull.
summary.zh: 转动，顺着磁铁吸力的方向。

detail.en:
A small, light magnet balanced on a point so that it can turn freely. Its north-pole half is coloured. Near a bar magnet it lines up with the curves of the iron filings; away from magnets it settles pointing north [S5].

In this model it swings for a few seconds before it comes to rest [S1].
detail.zh:
一根又小又轻的磁铁，支在一个尖上，能自由转动，北极那一半涂了颜色。靠近条形磁铁时，它顺着铁屑的弧线指；远离磁铁时，它指着北方停住 [S5]。

在这个模型里，它要摆几秒钟才停稳 [S1]。

summary.en: Keeps fingers and dust off the needle.
summary.zh: 挡住手指和灰尘，保护磁针。

detail.en: A clear cover over the needle, so that the needle can be read without touching it [S1].
detail.zh: 罩在磁针上的透明盖子，不用碰磁针就能读出它的方向 [S1]。

summary.en: Lets the bar magnet turn freely.
summary.zh: 让条形磁铁能自由转动。

detail.en:
A stand with a thin thread and a paper cradle for the bar magnet. Hung like this, the magnet can turn without being held or blocked: it is freely suspended [S2].

Away from other magnets it swings, slows and comes to rest pointing north and south [S2]. In this model north is towards the back of the bench [S1].
detail.zh:
支架上挂着一根细线和一个纸托，用来挂条形磁铁。这样挂着，磁铁不被握住、也不被挡住，能自由转动，这就是自由悬挂 [S2]。

远离其他磁铁时，它摆几下、慢下来，最后指着南北停住 [S2]。在这个模型里，北方朝着实验台的后面 [S1]。

summary.en: Holds the objects to test, and the card stand.
summary.zh: 放着待测物品；后面是卡片架。

detail.en:
A plastic tray of eight everyday objects made of different materials, all tested with the same magnet [S1].

Behind the paper, a steel stand holds the bar magnet over a chain of paper clips for the card test [S1].
detail.zh:
塑料盘里放着八件用不同材料做的日常物品，都用同一根磁铁来测试 [S1]。

纸的后面有一个钢支架，做卡片实验时，用它把条形磁铁夹在一串回形针上方 [S1]。

summary.en: Is attracted: iron is a magnetic material.
summary.zh: 被吸引：铁是磁性材料。

detail.en:
An iron nail is attracted by a magnet, even though it is not a magnet itself [S2].

Being attracted does not prove that an object is a magnet: only a push from a magnet’s pole shows that [S3].
detail.zh:
铁钉本身不是磁铁，却会被磁铁吸引 [S2]。

被吸引并不能证明一个物体是磁铁，只有被磁极推开才能证明 [S3]。

summary.en: Are attracted: steel is a magnetic material.
summary.zh: 被吸引：钢是磁性材料。

detail.en:
Three small clips bent from steel wire [S1]. Steel is a magnetic material, so a magnet picks them up [S2].

The same kind of clip is used for every count in this topic, so that the results can be compared [S2].
detail.zh:
三只用钢丝弯成的小回形针 [S1]。钢是磁性材料，磁铁能把它们吸起来 [S2]。

这一课的计数都用同一种回形针，结果才能互相比较 [S2]。

summary.en: Is attracted: the can is made of steel.
summary.zh: 被吸引：罐子是钢做的。

detail.en:
A small food can made of steel [S1]. A magnet attracts it [S2].

Steel and aluminium cans can look alike; a magnet tells them apart, and the same idea is used to pick steel out of scrap [S4].
detail.zh:
一个钢做的小罐头 [S1]。磁铁会吸引它 [S2]。

钢罐和铝罐看起来可能差不多，用磁铁一试就分得出来；从废料里挑出钢铁，用的也是这个道理 [S4]。

summary.en: Is not attracted: aluminium is non-magnetic.
summary.zh: 不被吸引：铝是非磁性材料。

detail.en:
The ring-pull tab from a drinks can, made of aluminium [S1]. Aluminium is a metal, but a magnet does not attract it [S20].

It shows that not every metal is a magnetic material [S20].
detail.zh:
饮料罐上的拉环，用铝做成 [S1]。铝是金属，但磁铁不吸引它 [S20]。

它说明不是所有金属都是磁性材料 [S20]。

summary.en: Is not attracted: copper is non-magnetic.
summary.zh: 不被吸引：铜是非磁性材料。

detail.en: A plain disc of solid copper, with nothing printed on it [S1]. Copper is a metal, but a magnet does not attract it [S20].
detail.zh: 一片素面的实心铜片 [S1]。铜是金属，但磁铁不吸引它 [S20]。

summary.en: Is hardly attracted, unlike ordinary steel.
summary.zh: 几乎不被吸引，和普通的钢不同。

detail.en:
The spoon in this model is made of austenitic stainless steel, a kind that a magnet hardly attracts [S9]. Other kinds of stainless steel, called ferritic and martensitic, are attracted [S9].

It was chosen to show that the word “steel” alone does not predict the result: test the object itself [S1].
detail.zh:
模型里的勺子是奥氏体不锈钢，磁铁几乎吸不动这一种 [S9]。另外几种不锈钢叫铁素体不锈钢和马氏体不锈钢，会被磁铁吸引 [S9]。

选它，是为了说明单看“钢”这个字不能判断结果，要拿物品本身来试 [S1]。

summary.en: Is not attracted: wood is non-magnetic.
summary.zh: 不被吸引：木头是非磁性材料。

detail.en: A small block of wood [S1]. A magnet does not attract it [S2], but a magnet’s pull passes through wood [S23].
detail.zh: 一小块木头 [S1]。磁铁不吸引它 [S2]，但磁铁的吸力能穿过木头 [S23]。

summary.en: Is not attracted: plastic is non-magnetic.
summary.zh: 不被吸引：塑料是非磁性材料。

detail.en: A short plastic ruler [S1]. A magnet does not attract it [S2].
detail.zh: 一把短塑料尺 [S1]。磁铁不吸引它 [S2]。

summary.en: Each card adds 2 mm between magnet and clips.
summary.zh: 每张卡片在磁铁和回形针之间加宽 2 mm。

detail.en:
Paper cards, each 2 mm thick in this design, held under the north pole of the clamped magnet [S1]. Paper is not a magnetic material, so the pull passes through, but each card widens the gap and weakens the pull [S23].

In this model, 0 to 6 cards let the magnet hold 10, 5, 3, 2, 1, 1 and 0 clips [S1]. The numbers are an example; the pattern is what matters.
detail.zh:
纸卡片，本设计每张厚 2 mm，夹在磁铁北极的下面 [S1]。纸不是磁性材料，吸力能穿过去，但每多一张，间隙就宽一些，吸力也弱一些 [S23]。

在这个模型里，隔着 0 到 6 张卡片，磁铁依次吸住 10、5、3、2、1、1、0 只回形针 [S1]。数字只是举例，重要的是规律。

summary.en: Shows how strong the pull is by the count.
summary.zh: 用吸住的只数表示吸力大小。

detail.en:
Identical steel paper clips hang one from another under the cards. The more clips the magnet holds, the stronger its pull through the cards [S1].

In this model the magnet holds a chain of ten clips with no cards in between [S1].
detail.zh:
一样的钢回形针一只挂一只，吊在卡片下面。磁铁吸住的回形针越多，说明它隔着卡片的吸力越大 [S1]。

在这个模型里，不夹卡片时，磁铁能吸住一串十只回形针 [S1]。

summary.en: Becomes a magnet when stroked one way.
summary.zh: 朝一个方向摩擦后，变成磁铁。

detail.en:
A steel needle, 80 mm long in this design [S1]. Stroked many times from end to end with the same pole of a magnet, always the same way and lifting the magnet clear in between, it becomes a magnet [S19].

In this model 0, 10, 20 and 30 strokes let it hold 0, 2, 4 and 6 clips [S1]. Real needles give different numbers.
detail.zh:
一根钢针，本设计长 80 mm [S1]。用磁铁的同一个磁极从一端摩擦到另一端，每次方向相同，中间把磁铁抬起来，摩擦许多次后，它就变成了磁铁 [S19]。

在这个模型里，摩擦 0、10、20、30 次，它依次能吸住 0、2、4、6 只回形针 [S1]。真的钢针会得出不同的数目。

summary.en: Show how strong the stroked needle is.
summary.zh: 显示摩擦后的钢针有多强。

detail.en: Steel paper clips picked up by the end of the needle. In this model 20 strokes give 4 clips and 30 strokes give 6 [S1].
detail.zh: 被钢针一端吸住的钢回形针。在这个模型里，摩擦 20 次吸住 4 只，30 次吸住 6 只 [S1]。

summary.en: Becomes a magnet while current flows.
summary.zh: 有电流流过线圈时，变成磁铁。

detail.en:
A 100 mm steel nail inside the coil [S1]. While current flows round the coil, the nail is a magnet; in this model it changes colour to show this [S4].

Steel keeps a little magnetism after the current stops, so in this model it still holds one clip. A soft iron core keeps almost none [S22].
detail.zh:
线圈里的一根 100 mm 钢钉 [S1]。电流绕着线圈流动时，钉子就是一块磁铁；在这个模型里，它会变色来表示这一点 [S4]。

电流停止后，钢还留着一点磁性，所以在这个模型里它仍吸住一只回形针。软铁芯几乎不留磁性 [S22]。

summary.en: Makes the nail a magnet when current flows.
summary.zh: 电流流过时，使钉子成为磁铁。

detail.en:
Thirty turns of insulated copper wire wound round the nail [S1]. Current flowing round the turns makes the nail inside a magnet [S4].

The coating on the wire stops neighbouring turns touching electrically, so the current goes round and round instead of taking a short cut [S8].
detail.zh:
绕在钉子上的 30 圈绝缘铜线 [S1]。电流一圈圈地流过，里面的钉子就成了磁铁 [S4]。

导线外面的绝缘皮让相邻的线圈不会接通，电流只能一圈一圈地绕，不会抄近路 [S8]。

summary.en: Push the current round the coil.
summary.zh: 推动电流流过线圈。

detail.en:
Two AA-size dry cells, 14.5 mm across and 50.5 mm long [S1]. In this model two batteries let the nail lift 6 clips and one battery lets it lift 3 [S1].

Use dry cells only: the coil and batteries get warm, so switch off between tests [S8].
detail.zh:
两节 AA 号干电池，直径 14.5 mm、长 50.5 mm [S1]。在这个模型里，两节电池让钉子吸起 6 只回形针，一节电池吸起 3 只 [S1]。

只用干电池：线圈和电池会发热，每次测完就断开开关 [S8]。

summary.en: Turns the electromagnet on and off.
summary.zh: 接通或断开电磁铁。

detail.en: A slide switch in the circuit [S1]. Closed, it completes the circuit and current flows; open, the current stops and the nail lets go of most of its clips [S2].
detail.zh: 电路里的一个拨动开关 [S1]。合上时电路接通，电流流动；断开时电流停止，钉子放下大部分回形针 [S2]。

summary.en: Join batteries, switch and coil in one loop.
summary.zh: 把电池、开关和线圈连成一个回路。

detail.en:
Insulated wires join the batteries, the switch and the coil in a closed loop [S1]. A steel stand holds the nail upright, with a few loose clips lying below it [S1].

The moving dots show the current, from the positive end of the batteries round to the negative end [S1].
detail.zh:
绝缘导线把电池、开关和线圈连成一个闭合的回路 [S1]。钢支架把钉子竖着夹住，下面散放着几只回形针 [S1]。

流动的小点表示电流，从电池的正极绕一圈回到负极 [S1]。

summary.en: Show how strong the electromagnet is.
summary.zh: 显示电磁铁有多强。

detail.en: Steel paper clips hanging from the tip of the nail [S1]. In this model two batteries hold 6, one battery holds 3, and with the switch open 1 stays [S1].
detail.zh: 挂在钉尖上的钢回形针 [S1]。在这个模型里，两节电池吸住 6 只，一节电池吸住 3 只，开关断开后还剩 1 只 [S1]。

summary.en: Has a steel front that magnets stick to.
summary.zh: 钢制门面，磁铁能吸在上面。

detail.en:
A cut-off piece of a fridge door, not a whole fridge [S1]. Its front is steel, so a fridge magnet sticks to it [S15].

The rubber seal round its edge has a magnetic strip inside [S15].
detail.zh:
截取的一段冰箱门，不是整台冰箱 [S1]。门面是钢做的，冰箱贴能吸在上面 [S15]。

门四周的橡胶门封里有一条磁条 [S15]。

summary.en: Pulls the door shut against the steel body.
summary.zh: 把门吸在钢制箱体上关紧。

detail.en:
A soft rubber seal runs round the inside edge of the door, with a flat magnetic strip inside it. The strip pulls the seal against the steel body of the fridge, so the door stays shut and the seal fits tightly [S15].

The seal’s shape is simplified in this model [S1].
detail.zh:
柔软的橡胶门封沿门的内侧绕一圈，里面有一条扁平的磁条。磁条把门封吸在冰箱的钢制箱体上，门就关得住，门封也贴得紧 [S15]。

模型把门封的形状画简单了 [S1]。

summary.en: Holds a note against the steel door.
summary.zh: 把便条吸在钢制门上。

detail.en: A thin, bendy magnet [S15]. It sticks to the steel door and holds a sheet of paper under it, because its pull passes through paper [S23].
detail.zh: 一块又薄又软的磁铁 [S15]。它吸在钢制的门上，还能压住一张纸，因为它的吸力能穿过纸 [S23]。

summary.en: Holds the cabinet door shut with a magnet.
summary.zh: 用磁铁吸住柜门。

detail.en:
A small magnet between two steel plates, fixed in the cabinet frame, attracts a steel plate on the door [S20]. The plate on the door has to be made of a magnetic material.

Beside it, two small models show bigger uses: a crane with a round lifting electromagnet [S4] and a maglev train held up by magnetic attraction under its track [S21]. They are teaching models, not to scale [S1].
detail.zh:
门框里固定着一块夹在两片钢片之间的小磁铁，吸住柜门上的一块钢片 [S20]。柜门上的这块片子必须用磁性材料做。

旁边两个小模型展示更大的用途：一台装着圆形起重电磁铁的起重机 [S4]，和一列靠轨道下方的磁吸引托起的磁浮列车 [S21]。它们是教学模型，没有按比例 [S1]。

summary.en: Show the pattern round the magnet.
summary.zh: 显出磁铁周围的图样。

detail.en:
Tiny bits of iron sprinkled on paper round the magnets. Each bit lines up with the magnet’s pull, and they crowd where the pull is strongest, at the poles [S7].

In this model the pattern is worked out from where the magnets are. The moving lines, when switched on, trace the same curves; they are a way of picturing the pattern [S5].
detail.zh:
撒在磁铁周围纸上的细小铁屑。每一粒都顺着磁铁吸力的方向排列，在吸力最强的磁极处挤得最密 [S7]。

在这个模型里，图样是按磁铁的位置算出来的。打开后流动的线描出同样的弧线，它们只是画出图样的方法 [S5]。

summary.en: Holds the equipment.
summary.zh: 摆放器材。

detail.en: Context only: a generic school bench, 90 × 50 cm in this design [S1]. A plastic guide strip lets bar magnet B slide in a straight line [S1].
detail.zh: 只是背景：通用的学校实验台，本设计 90 × 50 cm [S1]。一条塑料导轨让条形磁铁 B 沿直线滑动 [S1]。

summary.en: Gives the door seal a steel edge to grip.
summary.zh: 给门封一条能吸住的钢边。

detail.en: Context only: a cut-off piece of the fridge’s steel body, which the magnetic strip in the door seal is pulled against [S15].
detail.zh: 只是背景：截取的一段冰箱钢制箱体，门封里的磁条就吸在它上面 [S15]。

summary.en: Carries the steel plate for the catch.
summary.zh: 装着门扣用的钢片。

detail.zh: 只是背景：截取的一段橱柜门和搁板 [S1]。
